doc.title: James Moody — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Saxophone influences before Charlie Parker
summary: After hearing Parker he stopped searching; earlier players included Rudy Williams, Tab Smith and Bill Bostic.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: When you started on alto, who were some of the people -- You like Jimmy Dorsey (phonetic sp.). I remember you said that. Were there other players beside Jimmy Dorsey and Charlie Parker who were influences on you?

Charlie Parker was the last one I heard. That's why when I heard him, that was it. That was it, yeah. But there was a guy by the name of Rudy Williams (phonetic sp.) who played with the Savoy Salton (phonetic sp.) and he was from Newark. There was, I mean, there was like Tab Smith (phonetic sp.) with Count Bassie, but I, you know, like I kind of narrowed it down because all these guys they play nice saxophone, but that wasn't the way I wanted to play. Like Bill Bostic (phonetic sp.). Did you know that Bill Bostic was a better saxophonist than Charlie Parker?

They say, like, they say he was the better saxophonist, like he knew the instrument better, but I didn't like his -- the way he played, you know? I like Charlie Parker (indiscernible), you see? And there are a lot of people, you know, they know the instrument better than someone, but another person plays his better.

Like, man, I dug Lester Young (phonetic sp.), but Harper (phonetic sp.) played more changes, but I did that [sings], but man, that Harper [sings], he was whipping in between those changes. But see, that's, that's the thing. You have to live and learn and find out because the things that you think are great today like won't be too cool tomorrow. There's always something a little better, you know, if you're looking in the right direction, you know. But things that -- you know, there's always something better if you're looking for something to grow with. When you have a relationship with your wife, you make that grow and make that better tomorrow, you see, rather than thinking, well, now I'll find something better tomorrow. It doesn't do that way.
